findings.title: Promise-return documentation includes synchronous client methods
findings.reproduction: Run node docs/audits/AUD-006-harnesses/api-contract.mjs; it imports the actual client with synthetic package placeholders and calls only metadata methods and idle cancellation. No worker or KDF runs.
findings.expected: Document exactly which methods return a Promise: encrypt, decrypt, check, readPhrase and readContainer. Keep mode, maxSupportedMemLevel and cancel synchronous as their TypeScript signatures already declare.
findings.observed: Both API.md and web/README.md say Every method returns a promise. Actual mode() returns a string, maxSupportedMemLevel() returns 0, and cancel() returns undefined. A caller following the blanket .catch() advice for these methods gets a TypeError.
findings.impact: Low, documentation-only integration ambiguity. Actual operation methods correctly return rejected Promises; no cryptographic output or secret handling is affected.
evidence: web/client.d.ts already declares the synchronous return types
findings.recommendedFix: Replace Every method with an explicit list of the five asynchronous operation methods and state that metadata queries/cancel are synchronous. Do not change the working public API to satisfy the sentence.
findings.requiredVerification: Review both prose pages against client.d.ts and rerun api-contract.mjs; no expensive vector calculation is needed.

recommendations.text: Promote a self-contained reduced-cost Chromium/Firefox smoke suite into routine CI. Current CI exercises Emscripten under Node and a stand-in client worker; this audit adds actual Blob workers, CSP, transfer, cancellation and callback handling from the canonical archive. Avoid depending on a sibling checkout in the permanent CI version.
recommendations.disposition: Done in 7f5e8fb: scripts/verify-browsers.mjs runs dist/ in Chromium and Firefox with Playwright 1.63.0, as a file and from an isolated loopback server, at the reduced cost of REDUCED_COST_CONTAINER, without a sibling checkout; the CI check job runs it after check.sh.

recommendations.text: Explicitly say page callbacks must be synchronous, or deliberately implement and test Promise rejection handling. An async callback that rejects currently produces an unhandled rejection while the operation continues and can resolve. Existing wording promises handling when a callback throws, so this is recorded as a scope clarification, not a failure of the tested synchronous contract.
recommendations.disposition: Implemented in d343789: an async onProgress or onUnverified whose promise rejects while the operation runs stops it with CALLBACK_FAILED; a later rejection stays the page's unhandled one. Tested with the stand-in worker and in both real browsers. The async-callback.mjs probe, which recorded the earlier behaviour, now fails by design.

recommendations.text: Consider container-aware Linux limits (cgroup v2/v1) and configurable headroom; /proc/meminfo is a host estimate and a concurrent workload can invalidate it. Keep allocation failure explicit and never silently lower the work factor. Release the Mach host send right if memory estimation will be called repeatedly in long-lived integrations. No OOM or real macOS port-exhaustion experiment was performed.
recommendations.disposition: Done: 079a30081f568ab147baeae37a6957b0c8852fed lowers the Linux figure to the room left in the process's cgroup v2 or v1 group and its parents (checked with systemd-run -p MemoryMax=1G and docker run -m 1g); the same commit releases the Mach host send right after each query. The work factor is never lowered.

recommendations.text: For a future API revision, consider a validated mnemonic-length enum and constructors/getters for address network/type and search limits. They would make invalid combinations harder to construct; current operational paths validate lengths before KDF and use small search defaults. Avoid a breaking refactor solely for OOP style.
recommendations.disposition: Done: 0205a0a122491482461b5854e1dfc6ea280ffac7 adds WordCount (12, 15, 18, 21 or 24) for PhraseLength::Words and Reference::BuiltInCheck; the same commit makes the network and address type of a BitcoinAddress read-only and SearchLimits::new refuse counts outside 1 to 2^31.

recommendations.text: Describe the verifier as an internal consistency check, not password authentication; distinguish the 1024 normalized-byte password bound from longer valid pre-normalization input; update the argon2Engine cross-reference to web/argon2-engine.js. These are small clarity edits, not new algorithm findings.
recommendations.disposition: Done: d343789 (verifier as a consistency check; argon2Engine in web/argon2-engine.js) and 17c45ad (both password bounds at LINE_CAPACITY).

recommendations.text: Keep the present functional core and trait-based engine boundary. Large files contain substantial tests/help, so line counts alone do not justify splitting them. If these features grow, separate address parsing from BIP32 derivation and HTTP parsing from launcher selection at their existing function seams. Retain explicit cleanup and straightforward control flow.
recommendations.disposition: No change: the advice applies if these features grow, and they have not.
